processes.name: Calpine daily gas nomination receipt and confirmation
processes.description: Calpine's fuel supply contact emails a Word nomination document to the Enron logistics desk, usually after a phone call, with Daren Farmer and others copied. A scheduler acknowledges and confirms the volumes and path.
processes.stall_points: The nomination arrives as an attached .doc, often with no body text, so the scheduler re-keys it. The recipient changes from message to message, and the sender repeats that it was agreed by phone.
processes.automation: Parse the attached nomination into a structured nomination record and auto-acknowledge when volumes match the prior day. Only exceptions would go to a person.

evidence.quote: As we spoke about by phone, here is the nomination, Thanks.

Will be out Friday, will call if there are any changes.Thanks

processes.name: Customer and supplier nomination spreadsheets received by email
processes.description: Counterparties such as TXU, Reliant and the Enron methanol and MTBE plants email daily or monthly nominations and actuals as spreadsheet attachments. Logistics staff forward them to the desk and key them into scheduling.
processes.stall_points: Nominations arrive as attachments with no body text and are forwarded by hand. Each file has to be opened and re-keyed, and the same send repeats for every gas day.
processes.automation: Ingest the attachments, extract volumes by meter and day, and load them to the nomination system. Flag differences from the prior nomination.

evidence.quote: HPL Nomination for January 15 thru 17, 2000
Enron Methanol Company nominates the following requirements for the Methanol Plant for January 2000:
and I remembered to send these to you.....

processes.name: Missing or expired deal tickets chased from the Texas desk
processes.description: Volume management and scheduling staff find flow at a meter with no valid deal or contract. This includes expired Sitara deals, UA4 report items and new wells. They email Daren Farmer or the deal makers to extend, roll or create a ticket, often with a deadline tied to settlement or close.
processes.stall_points: Requests wait on one person to extend or create the deal and then get resent. Threads are forwarded with long quoted history. The same meter/month questions come back again (UA4 1998 items, Nov/Dec deals).
processes.automation: Auto-detect meters with flow but no active deal, and route a pre-filled ticket request with the meter, month and volume to the deal owner. Track open items with deadlines.

processes.name: Meter allocation exceptions and reallocation requests
processes.description: Volume management reviews meter allocations, exception reports and pipeline-versus-HPL volume discrepancies. They ask schedulers to move, zero out or reallocate volumes between contracts and packages for a past month, then confirm back.
processes.stall_points: The fix needs the right person to act in POPS or Unify, and a follow-up chaser if nobody answers. Corrections are requested after the month has flowed and sometimes ahead of close.
processes.automation: Surface allocation exceptions and pipeline-versus-internal mismatches automatically, and generate a standard reallocation request with before/after volumes. Log who confirmed the fix.

evidence.quote: Please make sure these volumes are moved off the Reliant contract prior to November close.
These were buybacks that were incorrectly nominated to transport contracts
This does show up on my meter exception report.  Please advise.
Meter 1517, Sweeny Phillips, has been reallocated for 12/99.

processes.name: Month-end Unify/Sitara close and bridge-back error clearing
processes.description: Each month a close schedule is circulated with fixed times for the Unify to Sitara bridge back, mass draft and accrual. Schedulers must clear bridge-back errors by the cutoff, which sends them asking deal owners which deal a meter belongs on.
processes.stall_points: Errors can only be cleared once someone supplies the right deal or volume, so schedulers chase against a hard clock time.
processes.automation: Send the close calendar automatically and list outstanding bridge-back errors by owner ahead of the cutoff. Suggest the likely deal from prior months.

processes.name: HL&P flow spreadsheet distribution and shortfall handling
processes.description: Kimberly Vaughn periodically emails the HL&P month-to-date flow spreadsheet to Janet Wallis, Daren and Howard Camp. Shortfall days are then discussed by email to decide whether to bill or buy back under the contract.
processes.stall_points: The spreadsheet is rebuilt and attached by hand each time with a one-line cover note. Shortfall treatment needs a human ruling from Janet.
processes.automation: Generate and send the HL&P month-to-date report on a schedule from the source data. Compute shortfalls against the 5% tolerance and show them in the report.

processes.name: Industrial accounts buyback and swing setup and handoff
processes.description: Industrial customer deals such as Valero and Lyondell need monthly buyback and swing tickets, correct ranking and buyback or force majeure decisions. Ken Seaman and then Robert Lloyd email the desk and volume management, and Daren and Pat chase deadlines and the Industrial spreadsheet.
processes.stall_points: Force majeure documentation or commercial decisions are awaited from traders, and the status has to be chased. Tickets are set up late in the month, so volume management reworks earlier months.
processes.automation: Create a monthly checklist with buyback and swing tickets per meter and due dates. Track pending commercial decisions. Distribute the Industrial worksheet automatically.

processes.name: Out-of-office coverage notices
processes.description: Staff email the group an out-of-office note naming who covers which pipelines, pools, confirmations and nominations while they are away. The notices are rewritten and sent to a long distribution list each time.
processes.stall_points: Coverage is communicated by free-text email, so the person covering a desk has to read and interpret it. Recipients are asked to forward it onward.
processes.automation: Keep a shared coverage roster that routes questions and scheduled tasks to the named backup when someone is marked out. This would remove the manual broadcast.

processes.name: Unassigned pathing and ownership gaps chased by the desk
processes.description: After desk reassignments, schedulers find deals left unpathed, nominations missing or pipelines with no owner. They list the open items by email and ask who is assigned, and management follows up with the group.
processes.stall_points: No one knows who owns a pipeline, so items stay unresolved across several weeks and the list is re-sent with status annotations.
processes.automation: Keep an owner registry per pipeline and zone, and flag unpathed deals each day to the named owner. Escalate automatically if they stay open.

processes.name: Monthly plan and cost-center allocation updates
processes.description: Management teams must return percentage allocations of their cost centers to finance for the plan and for monthly actuals. Updates are made in protected spreadsheets, and revisions are emailed back and forth with tight deadlines.
processes.stall_points: Protected cells block edits, so the spreadsheet is sent back for finance to fix. Each manager's input is requested with short deadlines.
processes.automation: Provide a shared allocation form with validation that the totals equal 100%. Prefill the prior month and collect submissions centrally.

evidence.quote: I need each of you to review the 2000 Plan allocations as I submitted them earlier today, and provide an accurate allocation of your RC for 1/00.

processes.name: Pipeline outage and shut-in notices and supply negotiation
processes.description: Gas control and field staff announce meter shut-ins and line work, and logistics staff then work out what to do with affected nominations. That can mean negotiating with the producer to hold gas or sending written notices through the deal makers.
processes.stall_points: Notices are forwarded through several people before the right contact is reached. Follow-up requests ask for a quick answer.
processes.automation: Match shut-in meter lists against open nominations and notify the affected schedulers and counterparties automatically.

evidence.quote: Rather than cut these volumes, would you try to negotiate with Koch not to flow this gas during the outage
